intro.html: These are copy-paste starting points, not legal advice — fill in the brackets, then paste the text into a contact form or email. Swap out anything that doesn't apply to your situation.

blocks.text:
To the Privacy Team,

I am requesting that you remove my personal information from your website and services. I do not consent to the collection, storage, or display of my data.

Name: [Your Full Name]
Also known as: [Any previous names/aliases]
Current address: [Your current address]
Former addresses: [List any former addresses you know are listed]
Phone number: [Your phone number]
Email addresses: [All email addresses you've used]

Please confirm in writing when my data has been removed.

Sincerely,
[Your Full Name]
[Date]
blocks.before: Copy and paste this into contact forms or emails.

blocks.label: Tip
blocks.html: Many data brokers have a dedicated opt-out form. Check their footer for "Do Not Sell My Info" or "Privacy Request" links first.

blocks.text:
Subject: Data Removal Request Under [GDPR / CCPA]

To the Privacy Team,

I am exercising my rights under [GDPR Article 17 / CCPA Section 1798.105] to request the deletion of my personal information from your systems.

I request that you:
- Delete all personal information you hold about me
- Delete any derived data or profiles about me
- Direct any third parties who hold my data to delete it as well

My information:

Name: [Your Full Name]
Email: [Your email address]
Additional identifiers: [Account numbers, usernames, etc.]

Please acknowledge receipt of this request and confirm deletion within the required [30 days / 45 days] timeframe.

Sincerely,
[Your Full Name]
[Date]
blocks.before: Use this if the company is based in the EU (GDPR) or California (CCPA).

blocks.label: Note
blocks.html: This works best for companies based in the EU or California. Many US-based companies will ignore GDPR requests.

Google will automatically handle the request through their tool, but you may need to manually submit for certain results.

Request URL: myactivity.google.com/results-about-you

items.text: Add the personal information you want to monitor
When Google finds a result, click "Request removal"
Google will review and remove if it "meets policy requirements"

blocks.label: Google's policy
blocks.html: They will remove results that are "doxxing" or "unwanted" but may not remove public records or news articles.
